title: Review of Lessons 4–7: الْمَفْعُول بِهِ, كَانَ as the Mirror of إِنَّ, and the Terms مَرْفُوع، مَنْصُوب، مَجْرُور
summary: Continuing the revision, the class settles the negation rules and لِأَنَّ, then takes up lesson five's central concept, الْمَفْعُول بِهِ — the object of a verb, which carries a fatḥa — along with the verbs that take no object at all and the rule that a verb placed before a plural doer stays singular. Lesson seven brings كَانَ, which the teacher frames as the exact mirror of إِنَّ: where إِنَّ puts the مُبْتَدَأ in the accusative, كَانَ does that to the خَبَر.
key_points: مَا negates the مَاضِي and لَا the مُضَارِع as a general rule; there are specific circumstances where each crosses over, to be covered later.

لِأَنَّ (li-anna : because) is أَنَّ with a lām attached and behaves as one of the sisters of إِنَّ. The technical name for the whole family is الْأَحْرُف الْمُشَبَّهَة بِالْفِعْل (al-aḥruf al-mushabbahah bi-l-fiʿl : the particles resembling verbs).

The مُبْتَدَأ affected by إِنَّ is not always the immediately following word — إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ … لَآيَاتٍ shows the fatḥa landing further on, which is why the rule is stated in terms of the مُبْتَدَأ rather than the next word.
A plural of something غَيْر عَاقِل (ghayr ʿāqil : without intellect) is treated as a feminine singular, so النَّوَافِذ is referred to as فَتَحْتُهَا.
الْمَفْعُول بِهِ (al-mafʿūl bihi : the direct object) takes a fatḥa — حَفِظْتُ سُورَةَ الْفَجْرِ, because the memorising is being done to the sūrah.
Not every verb takes an object. جَلَسَ (to sit) is done to nothing, so it has no مَفْعُول; you may state where someone sat, but that is not the thing acted upon.

There are several kinds of مَفْعُول — بِهِ، فِيهِ (which is الظَّرْف), لِأَجْلِهِ، مَعَهُ — and مَفْعُول بِهِ is the technical name for the object. Since it is the only one met so far, it is usually just called the مَفْعُول.
The habit to build: on seeing a verb, immediately look for its فَاعِل, which takes a ḍamma, and its مَفْعُول, which takes a fatḥa.
When the verb precedes a plural doer it stays singular — ذَهَبَ الطُّلَّابُ إِلَى الْمَلْعَبِ — though reversed, الطُّلَّابُ ذَهَبُوا takes the plural verb.
A pronoun attached to the end of a verb is itself the object, so nothing further needs the fatḥa: فَتَحْتُ الْبَابَ becomes فَتَحْتُهُ.
كَانَ (kāna : was) is the mirror image of إِنَّ — إِنَّ puts the مُبْتَدَأ into the accusative, كَانَ does so to the خَبَر: إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ against وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا.
كَانَ has nothing to change when the خَبَر is a جَارّ وَمَجْرُور such as فِي الْفَصْلِ, since the preposition has already set that word's ending.

The formal iʿrāb terms are مَرْفُوع (marfūʿ : raised, carrying a ḍamma), مَنْصُوب (manṣūb : carrying a fatḥa), and مَجْرُور (majrūr : carrying a kasra) — the last being the root of حَرْف الجَرّ. A word may be مَنْصُوب while its marker is a kasra, as with جَمْع الْمُؤَنَّث السَّالِم, where one says عَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الْكَسْرَة.
فَرِحَ بِ (fariḥa bi) is how to say pleased with something — فَفَرِحَ بِي الْمُدَرِّسُ, the teacher was pleased with me.
اسْم التَّفْضِيل as مُضَاف gives the superlative: إِنَّكَ أَحْسَنُ طَالِبٍ فِي الْفَصْلِ is the best student, not merely a better one, because there is no مِن.
هَاتِ (hāti : give me) has the feminine هَاتِي and plural هَاتُوا; خُذْ (khudh : take) is a command, though فِعْل الْأَمْر proper comes in the lesson after the test.
جَوْعَان (hungry) pluralises as جِيَاع, and عَطْشَان (thirsty) and شَبْعَان (full) follow the same pattern. لِمَ is simply the short form of لِمَاذَا.

Vocabulary: كَوَى يَكْوِي (to iron) with مِكْوَاة (an iron), جَوَاب with its plural أَجْوِبَة, غِلَاف (cover) and أَصْفَر (yellow), عَصِير بُرْتُقَال (orange juice), and أَبْشِرْ (rejoice), said when giving good news.
questions: [00:02:00] Q: Does the مُبْتَدَأ always come directly after إِنَّ? — A: Not necessarily, as إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ shows; stating the rule in terms of the مُبْتَدَأ keeps it accurate.
[00:04:00] Q: Why is النَّوَافِذ treated as feminine? — A: Because it is a plural of something غَيْر عَاقِل, and such plurals are handled as a feminine singular — hence فَتَحْتُهَا.

[00:08:00] Q: What is the difference between الْمَفْعُول and الْمَفْعُول بِهِ? — A: There are several types of مَفْعُول — بِهِ، فِيهِ، لِأَجْلِهِ، مَعَهُ — and بِهِ names the direct object; since it is the only one learned so far, it is loosely called just the مَفْعُول.
[00:13:00] Q: Is طُلَّاب also the plural for a group of female students? — A: No, that is طَالِبَات, and the book gives the feminine form right beside the masculine.
[00:15:00] Q: Why can't إِنَّكَ أَحْسَنُ طَالِبٍ be translated as a better student? — A: Because there is no مِن; as a مُضَاف the اسْم التَّفْضِيل carries the superlative sense, the best.
[00:17:00] Q: What is the يَاء doing in فَفَرِحَ بِي? — A: It is the ضَمِير for oneself, as in كِتَابِي, so the sentence means the teacher was pleased with me.
[00:25:01] Q: Where does هَاتُوا occur in the Qur'ān? — A: In هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ — bring your proof.

[00:26:00] Q: What do مَرْفُوع and مَجْرُور mean? — A: مَرْفُوع is the raised state carrying a ḍamma and مَجْرُور carries a kasra, which is where حَرْف الجَرّ gets its name; saying it takes a ḍamma or a kasra is just the simpler way of putting it.
[00:29:01] Q: Why answer بَلَى rather than نَعَمْ? — A: Because the question was did you not go; نَعَمْ would confirm the negative, so بَلَى is needed to affirm.
[00:32:00] Q: Where does يَمْشِي occur in the Qur'ān? — A: Early in Sūrat al-Baqarah, and in مَا لِهَذَا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشِي فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ.
[00:41:00] Q: Doesn't or always imply a question? — A: No. أَوْ is used outside questions, as in go to the park or the masjid; أَمْ belongs to the question offering two options.

quiz.q: What ending does الْمَفْعُول بِهِ take?
quiz.a: The object of the verb is مَنْصُوب — حَفِظْتُ سُورَةَ الْفَجْرِ, where the sūrah is what the memorising is done to.

quiz.q: Why does جَلَسَ take no مَفْعُول?
options: Because it is a past-tense verb
Because sitting is not done to anything
quiz.a: The teacher's example of a verb with no object: you may say where someone sat, but that place is not the thing acted upon.

quiz.q: Which is correct when the verb precedes a plural doer?
quiz.a: With the verb in front, it stays singular — the rule on page 33 the class kept returning to.

quiz.q: In فَتَحْتُهُ, what is the object of the verb?
options: An understood الْبَاب that must still take a fatḥa
quiz.a: A pronoun attached to the verb is itself the مَفْعُول, so no further word needs the fatḥa.

quiz.q: How does كَانَ differ from إِنَّ in its grammatical effect?
options: Both put the مُبْتَدَأ in the accusative
إِنَّ affects the مُبْتَدَأ, كَانَ affects the خَبَر
إِنَّ affects the خَبَر, كَانَ affects the مُبْتَدَأ
quiz.a: The teacher called كَانَ the opposite of إِنَّ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ against وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا.

quiz.q: Why does كَانَ leave فِي الْفَصْلِ untouched as a خَبَر?
options: Because the preposition فِي has already set that word's ending
quiz.a: When the خَبَر is a جَارّ وَمَجْرُور there is no fatḥa to give — the حَرْف الجَرّ has already made the word مَجْرُور.
مَجْرُور is the state of carrying a kasra, and it shares its root with حَرْف الجَرّ.

quiz.q: A word can be مَنْصُوب while showing a kasra. In which case does this happen?
quiz.a: With the sound feminine plural one says عَلَامَةُ نَصْبِهِ الْكَسْرَة — it is accusative, but marked by a kasra, as in خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ.

quiz.q: How do you say pleased with something?
quiz.a: فَرِحَ بِ — as in فَفَرِحَ بِي الْمُدَرِّسُ and the Qur'ānic فَرِحُوا بِمَا عِنْدَهُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ.

quiz.q: What is the plural form of هَاتِ?
quiz.a: هَاتِ for a male, هَاتِي for a female, and هَاتُوا for a group — the form in هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ.

quran_examples.arabic: إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ
quran_examples.transliteration: inna fī khalqi al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi wa-khtilāfi al-layli wa-l-nahāri la-āyātin li-ulī al-albāb
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's proof that the word affected by إِنَّ is not always the one immediately following it — here the مُبْتَدَأ comes much later in the āyah.

quran_examples.translation: And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.
quran_examples.note: Set directly against إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ to show the mirror rule: كَانَ puts the خَبَر into the accusative while leaving اللَّهُ raised.

quran_examples.translation: They were content with what they had of knowledge.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's example for the construction فَرِحَ بِ, meaning pleased with something.

quran_examples.arabic: فَرِحِينَ بِمَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ
quran_examples.transliteration: fariḥīna bi-mā ātāhumu llāhu min faḍlih
quran_examples.translation: Rejoicing in what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty.
quran_examples.note: A second instance of فَرِحَ بِ, cited in connection with the شُهَدَاء who are alive with their Lord.

quran_examples.arabic: خُذْهَا وَلَا تَخَفْ ۖ سَنُعِيدُهَا سِيرَتَهَا الْأُولَىٰ
quran_examples.transliteration: khudhhā wa-lā takhaf, sa-nuʿīduhā sīratahā al-ūlā
quran_examples.translation: Take it and fear not; We will return it to its former state.
quran_examples.note: Quoted for the command خُذْ, spoken to Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام about the staff that had become a snake; it also carries the future سَـ.

quran_examples.arabic: قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
quran_examples.transliteration: qul hātū burhānakum in kuntum ṣādiqīn
quran_examples.translation: Say: Produce your proof, if you should be truthful.
quran_examples.note: A student's answer for the plural هَاتُوا, and بُرْهَانَكُمْ here is a مَفْعُول بِهِ carrying the fatḥa.

quran_examples.arabic: وَقَالُوا مَالِ هَٰذَا الرَّسُولِ يَأْكُلُ الطَّعَامَ وَيَمْشِي فِي الْأَسْوَاقِ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-qālū mā-li hādhā al-rasūli yaʾkulu al-ṭaʿāma wa-yamshī fī al-aswāq
quran_examples.translation: And they said: What is this messenger, who eats food and walks in the markets?
quran_examples.note: Given for يَمْشِي, and الطَّعَامَ in it is a clean مَفْعُول بِهِ with the fatḥa, beside يَمْشِي which takes no object at all.
